# Two branches add different secrets. The paths are disjoint (no tree conflict);
# the audit-log merge combines both secret.add entries.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

# Stash secret contents outside the worktree (sesam's clean wipes untracked
# files under the sesam dir).
cp alpha.txt $TMPDIR/alpha.txt
cp beta.txt $TMPDIR/beta.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# OURS: add secret alpha.
exec git checkout -b ours
cp $TMPDIR/alpha.txt alpha
exec sesam add alpha --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add alpha'

# THEIRS: add secret beta.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
cp $TMPDIR/beta.txt beta
exec sesam add beta --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: add beta'

# Merge: the driver merges the log and reports a conflict (exit 1) so git stops.
# (sesam.yml also conflicts - accepted for now.)
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stdout 'merged it automatically'

# Finalize: reseal so the terminal seal covers the merged object set (this is the
# step the exit-1 merge forces the user to run before committing).
exec sesam seal --verify-mode no-disk

# Both secret.add entries survive in the merged log, which now verifies on disk.
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout 'alpha'
stdout 'beta'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'

-- alpha.txt --
alpha secret
-- beta.txt --
beta secret
